name: Shaphan
overview: Shaphan was a prominent scribe during King Josiah's reign, entrusted with important royal commands alongside his son Ahikam and others, demonstrating his influential role in Judah's governance (2 Kings 22:12; 2 Chronicles 34:20). He was also the father of several notable figures, including Ahikam, Elasah, Jaazaniah, and Gemariah, linking him to key events such as the protection of the prophet Jeremiah and diplomatic missions to Babylon (Jeremiah 26:24; 29:3). Additionally, Shaphan's family legacy continued through his grandson Gedaliah, who was appointed ruler over the remnant in Judah after the Babylonian exile, underscoring the enduring leadership role of his lineage (2 Kings 25:22).
